caption:
Followers is the number you show people. Sends per reach is the number that pays you.

Follower count tells you about your past — who found you at some point and never got round to unfollowing. It does not predict reach, and it does not predict revenue. Reach now depends on how people interact with what you post, not how many followers you have.

Sends per reach tells you something about right now: of the people who saw this, how many thought it was worth putting in front of a specific friend. That's the closest free proxy you have for "is this actually good", and it's the signal Mosseri says matters most for reaching people who don't follow you.

If you track one thing for the next 30 days, track that.

It's uncomfortable at first, because it's usually low and it can't be inflated. Which is exactly why it's useful — it's the only number on your dashboard that nobody can buy.
